learning: Across eleven iterations, the only large gain came from the Iteration 1 drivetrain step. Sensor footprint, count, lead, mass and track tests each matched or lost to it. The remaining off-track limit (max_error about 0.061 to 0.068 m against a 0.06 m floor) lies in the controller's response to excursions.
notes: Final package: the Iteration 1 geometry and controller, unchanged. This is the best-measured design (114.39), and it is the one carried to the unseen-track race.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the package reproduces the best-measured design exactly: Iteration 1 (score 114.39, oval progress 0.47, s-bend progress 0.26). Its geometry and controller were never beaten. Iteration 2 (7 sensors, 16 mm) fell to 65.7. Iteration 3 (8 mm footprint) gave 102.8. Iteration 4 (mass 0.5, radius 0.04, length 0.12, base 1.8) gave 110.2 with oscillation up to 0.33. Iteration 5 (lead 0.02 m) gave 91.8. Iteration 6 (lead 0.04 m) gave 109.9. Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.11) gave 107.6 and cost progress. Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.09) gave 113.36. Iteration 9 (mass 0.8) gave 106.0, and Iteration 10 (mass 0.5) gave 103.7. Every change tested from Iteration 1 either lost score or left it flat, so I keep the controller unchanged. Its gains (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.30, base 1.5, antisymmetric weights, last_direction) are the ones that produced the measured result. Any new controller gain would be untested on the unseen track and could only add risk. The observation request covers all measurements so the final result can be compared with Iteration 1 in full.
